messages:
mara: quick sync — i'm sketching guardrails for routing policy by plan (free/pro/enterprise). main goals: predictable SLAs, clear fallback order, and safe quota enforcement.

yusuf: sounds good. are we leaning hard quota (reject) vs soft grace (allow+telemetry) per plan?

mara: propose soft grace for free/pro, hard for enterprise by default. soft grace emits metrics + adds penalty headers so apps can degrade gracefully.

anya: +1. need a clear UX for support to temporarily lift quotas for troubleshooting. must be auditable and limited in scope/time.

pm-zoe: can we allow timeboxed overrides only for ops role, and require a two-step confirmation in console? otherwise we get accidental cost spikes.

infra-sre: agree. also need region-aware fallbacks — if eu-capacity is low, route to eu-small variant first, then us variant, not jump straight to lower-quality variant.

yusuf: here's a minimal example config i mocked for discussion:```yaml
routing_policy:
  tiers:
    free:
      fallback_order: [gpt-small, gpt-tiny]
      soft_grace_tokens: 500
      hard_quota_tokens: 10000
    pro:
      fallback_order: [gpt-base, gpt-optimized]
      soft_grace_tokens: 2000
      hard_quota_tokens: 100000
    enterprise:
      fallback_order: [gpt-optimized, gpt-base]
      soft_grace_tokens: 0
      hard_quota_tokens: 10000000
# override example (timeboxed):
overrides:
  - tenant: tenant-123
    role_allowed: [ops]
    actions: [bump_quota, change_fallback]
    expires_at: 2026-04-01T18:00:00Z
```

mara: nice. we should also include policy-level telemetry hooks: `routing.fallback.count`, `routing.fallback.latency_delta`, `quota.soft_violation.count`, `policy.override.requested`, `policy.override.approved_by`.

anya: UX note: in console rollouts page show a timeline: current policy + active overrides (with expiry) + an option to request ad-hoc override that creates a ticket for ops. audit link should be first-class.

infra-sre: thoughts on enforcement mode? i prefer `soft_then_hard` where soft violations are allowed for X seconds then auto-enforced to hard if continuous. this avoids flapping on bursty traffic.

pm-zoe: that fits product needs. add a per-tenant burst window config (seconds) plus max-burst-tokens.

yusuf: small API debate: current policy schema is flat JSON. if we add expressions (region == 'eu' && load > 0.8) we get more power but also complexity. do we want a v2 policy language or stick to composable primitives (regions, variants, quotas)?

mara: prefer primitives first to keep auditability and simple evaluation. we can add a limited condition language later but gate it behind enterprise and extra review.

infra-sre: also add `capacity_hint` field so routing doesn't pick a variant that would overload a pool (helps graceful degrade).

deploy-bot: deploy queued: policy-service schema v1.3 -> staging (build 0.3.7).

anya: action items: (1) yusuf to PR a policy schema draft (primitives-only) + example config. (2) mara to draft console UX for timeboxed overrides. (3) infra-sre to write telemetry contract with metrics and tags. (4) pm-zoe to validate with product & support. target sync next Wed.

mara: thanks — let's keep the fallback behavior conservative: prefer regional variant swapping before dropping model quality. log every fallback with tenant_id, tier, chosen_variant, reason.

pm-zoe: and include a dashboard mock that surfaces soft_violation trends and override churn per tenant.

yusuf: will start PR today. will add tests for policy evaluation order and burst window respecting.

mara: perfect. if anyone has corner cases (eg hybrid private tenants with dedicated pools) drop them here and we'll include in spec.
